evidence_tier: executed differential (tier 1), against the OpenMS4 Linux x86_64 Release C++ build
method: An oracle driver linked against the Release install at /ceph/ibmi/abi/oliver/opt/openms4-release-bc9cc12-c19e494-174b576 (conda-forge x86_64-conda-linux-gnu-g++ 14.4.0, libOpenMS core flags -O3 -DNDEBUG -std=gnu++23 -mssse3 -ffp-contract=off) on ibminode06 calls StringUtils::toInt32, toFloat and toDouble on 82 edge inputs and ProteinIdentification::sort on seven hits with tied scores in both directions. It ran twice in fresh processes with a clean environment; both runs agreed byte for byte (results/differ.txt empty). Doubles are printed with %.17g, floats with %.9g, NaN as nan or -nan by its sign bit, and a thrown ConversionError as ERR:<what()>. This run is what made the port follow libstdc++'s std::from_chars: a nonzero literal that rounds to zero is a conversion error there, and nan(n-char-sequence) is accepted after a minus sign; the earlier behaviour followed the libc++ strtod fallback, which the Linux build does not compile.
